formats.key: PermitWitnessTransferFrom(TokenPermissions permitted,address spender,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,LimitOrder witness)LimitOrder(OrderInfo info,address inputToken,uint256 inputAmount,OutputToken[] outputs)OrderInfo(address reactor,address swapper,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline,address additionalValidationContract,bytes additionalValidationData)OutputToken(address token,uint256 amount,address recipient)TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)
effects: The signer signs a one-time Permit2 authorization: the spender (the UniswapX reactor) can take up to permitted.amount of permitted.token from the signer, until the deadline, using a Permit2 nonce.
When a filler fills the order, inputAmount of inputToken leaves the signer and goes to the filler (the reactor builds the permit from the order, so permitted must equal the input).
For each output, the recipient receives at least the stated amount of the output token from the filler; the zero address means native currency.
An optional additionalValidationContract can block the fill. It moves none of the signer's assets.
formats.shown: Intent 'UniswapX Limit Order', with a raw spender, the allowance amount, the input amount sent, each output's minimum amount with its token and a raw recipient, and the permit expiry date.

findings.title: LimitOrder intent 'UniswapX Limit Order' does not say which token is sold and which is bought.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json, display.formats: "intent": "UniswapX Limit Order", and there is no interpolatedIntent. The swap terms are only in the fields 'Send' and 'Min amount to receive'.
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent like "Sell {witness.inputAmount} for at least {witness.outputs.[0].amount}", or change the intent to "Limit order: sell token for token".

findings.title: LimitOrder shows the spender as a raw address, so the signer cannot tell it is the UniswapX reactor.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json, field {"path": "spender", "label": "Approve to spender", "format": "raw"}; case 0 shows 'Approve to spender: 0xE592427A0AEce92De3Edee1F18E0157C05861564'.

findings.title: LimitOrder shows each output recipient as a raw address, so the signer cannot easily see it is their own wallet.
LimitOrder test messages are signatures UniswapX would reject: their nonce, deadline and spender differ from the order.
findings.evidence: cases/0.json: nonce 9876543210 vs witness.info.nonce 4242424242; deadline 1777600000 vs witness.info.deadline 1777000000; the spender 0xE592427A... is the Uniswap V3 SwapRouter, not a reactor. The reactor builds the permit from order.info.nonce and order.info.deadline, so the signature cannot verify.
findings.fix: Use consistent values in the test cases: nonce = witness.info.nonce, deadline = witness.info.deadline, spender = witness.info.reactor = a real UniswapX LimitOrderReactor address.

findings.title: LimitOrder shows the same amount twice, as 'Amount allowance' and as 'Send'.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json fields permitted.amount 'Amount allowance' and witness.inputAmount 'Send'; case 0 shows '1000 USDC' for both. The reactor requires permitted to equal the input.
findings.fix: Keep only the 'Send' field, or relabel 'Amount allowance' as 'Max amount spender can take'.

findings.title: LimitOrder hides witness.info, which holds the reactor, the swapper and an optional contract that can block the fill.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json field {"label": "Witness Info", "path": "witness.info", "visible": "never"}. The swapper must be the signer, and the reactor must equal the spender, which is shown.

couldNotCheck: Permit2 (0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3) source is not in the directory (the Sourcify fetch failed: contracts/COLLECT-FAILED.txt). The domain and the type string were checked from public knowledge, not from source.

The UniswapX LimitOrderReactor (the spender that uses the witness) has no source in the directory. How it binds permitted, nonce and deadline to the order, and any fee outputs it adds, were checked from public knowledge only.
